findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical interval-scheduling greedy solution: it sorts by right endpoint, fires at the earliest possible endpoint, and adds an arrow only when the next closed interval starts beyond the current coordinate. The implementation is compact, conventional, and expert interview quality, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 452 and a runnable Python interval contract. The manifest's O(n log n) time and O(n) space claims correctly account for endpoint sorting and Python's sorting workspace, and the source handles the app's defensive empty-list extension without affecting the native nonempty domain.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064921277. Its empty guard, in-place right-endpoint sort, initial arrow count and coordinate, closed-interval reuse test, and update on a disjoint interval are identical to the protected app-local algorithm and data flow; only type syntax and the LeetCode class wrapper differ.

The 31-, 127-, and 511-interval reverse-ordered disjoint tiers span more than 16x and require every balloon to start a new greedy group after sorting. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.97x the reference runtime. A correct repeated-minimum-and-filter control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 164.36x.

The Approach exactly matches the protected target and supplies the essential exchange argument for choosing the earliest ending balloon's endpoint. It correctly explains closed-endpoint reuse, the O(n log n) sort and O(n) scan, Python sorting space, the defensive empty guard, and the relevant alternative strategies and interval boundaries.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It restores the wall and unknown-y-coordinate model, unlimited vertically traveling arrows, inclusive endpoint rule, all three exact examples with every stated arrow coordinate and affected interval, and all three constraints in source order.
